newsitem.title: FRANCE: Homeless paper fined for anti-Jewish remarks.
newsitem.headline: Homeless paper fined for anti-Jewish remarks.

text.p: A Paris court on Tuesday fined the editor of a newspaper run by the homeless 20,000 francs ($4,000) for insulting Jews and freemasons.

George Mathis, 63, founder of Le Reverbere (Street Lamp), a paper sold on the street by the homeless, must also pay a symbolic one franc each to the plaintiffs -- the League Against Racism and Anti-Semitism (LICRA) and the Grand Orient de France freemason organisation.

Mathis, whose editorial took issue with the influence of Jews and freemasons in the judiciary, told the court at last month's hearing: "Le Reverbere says out loud what everyone thinks quietly. If the Jews have a problem, they should talk about it in public."
The French government has proposed legislation to strengthen anti-racism laws and toughen punishment for racist statements.
